source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 8 (PDF 174-191, printed 171-188); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 8 (Physical Optics and Gravitational Waves), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The two major areas of physics dealt with in this chapter are:

options.text: polarization of transverse waves and gravitational waves

blocks.explanation: The chapter deals with polarization of transverse waves and gravitational waves (8.1).

book_ref.quote: This chapter deals with two major areas of physics namely polarization of transverse waves

blocks.prompt: 2 Interference and diffraction of light prove that light:
blocks.explanation: Interference and diffraction prove the wave nature of light but do not tell whether the waves are longitudinal or transverse (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Interference and diffraction effects prove the wave nature of light.

blocks.prompt: 3 Which phenomenon shows that light waves are transverse in character?
blocks.explanation: Polarization of light suggests that light waves are transverse (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Polarization of light suggests that the light waves are transverse in character.

blocks.prompt: 4 In a transverse mechanical wave on a stretched string, the particles of the medium vibrate:

options.text: opposite to the direction of propagation
in circles along the direction of propagation
perpendicular to the direction of propagation

blocks.explanation: In transverse waves the vibrations of the particles are perpendicular to the direction of propagation (8.1).

book_ref.quote: the vibrations of the particles of the medium are perpendicular to the direction of propagation

blocks.prompt: 5 The plane of polarization is the plane containing:

options.text: the magnetic field and the source
the direction of vibration and the direction of propagation

blocks.explanation: The plane of polarization contains the direction of vibration of the particles and the direction of propagation (8.1).

book_ref.quote: The plane of polarization is the plane containing the direction of vibration

blocks.prompt: 6 In a light wave produced by an oscillating charge, the electric field vector E and the magnetic field vector B are:

options.text: at right angle to each other

blocks.explanation: A light wave consists of periodic variations of E accompanied by B at right angle to each other (8.1).

book_ref.quote: accompanied by the magnetic field vector B at right angle to each other

blocks.prompt: 7 Light which has components of vibration in all possible planes is called:
blocks.explanation: Ordinary light has vibrations in all possible planes; such light is unpolarized (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Ordinary light has components of vibration in all possible planes.

blocks.prompt: 8 Light is said to be polarized when its vibrations are:
blocks.explanation: If the vibrations are confined only in one plane, the light is polarized (8.1).

book_ref.quote: if the vibrations are confined only in one plane, the light is said to be polarized

blocks.prompt: 9 Which one of the following is NOT listed as a source of unpolarized light?
blocks.explanation: Sunlight, incandescent and fluorescent bulbs, candles and fire give unpolarized light; light through polarizing sunglasses is linearly polarized (8.1, 8.2).

book_ref.quote: Examples of unpolarized light sources are sunlight, incandescent light bulbs

blocks.prompt: 10 Polarization cannot occur for:
blocks.explanation: Polarization is shown by transverse waves only; it does not occur for longitudinal waves such as sound (8.1).

book_ref.quote: It does not occur for longitudinal waves such as sound waves.

blocks.prompt: 11 Polarization is the process by which the electric and magnetic vibrations of light waves are:

options.text: restricted to a single plane of vibration

blocks.explanation: Polarization restricts the electric and magnetic vibrations of light to a single plane (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Polarization is the process by which the electric and magnetic vibrations of light waves are restricted

blocks.prompt: 12 Which of these is NOT a method of polarizing unpolarized light mentioned in the chapter?

options.text: Passing light through a plain glass lens
Passing light through a polaroid sheet
Using crystals such as calcite or quartz

blocks.explanation: The methods listed are a polarizing filter (polaroid sheet), a polarizing beam splitter, and optical crystals like calcite and quartz (8.1).

book_ref.quote: Employing certain optical crystals or materials

blocks.prompt: 13 When unpolarized light passes through a polarizing filter, the electric field vectors that pass through are those:

options.text: perpendicular to the axis of the filter
at 45° to the axis of the filter
parallel to the axis of the filter

blocks.explanation: Only the electric field vector parallel to the axis of the filter passes; all others are blocked (8.1).

book_ref.quote: only that electric field vector which is parallel to the axis of polarized filter

blocks.prompt: 14 The most common method of polarizing unpolarized light is:

options.text: reflecting it from a rough wall
passing it through a polarizing filter

blocks.explanation: The most common method is passing the light through a polarizing filter such as a polaroid sheet (8.1).

book_ref.quote: The most common method by which an unpolarized light can be polarized

blocks.prompt: 15 The basis of polarization is the orientation, in a specific direction, of the light wave's:
blocks.explanation: The orientation of the electric field vector E in a specific direction is the basis of polarization (8.1).

book_ref.quote: The orientation of the electric field vector E of light waves in a specific direction

blocks.prompt: 16 When the electric field vector of light oscillates in a single plane, the light is:
blocks.explanation: Oscillation of E in a single plane is linear polarization (8.2).

book_ref.quote: When the electric field vector oscillates in a single plane

blocks.prompt: 17 Light passing through polarizing sunglasses is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Light passing through a polarizing filter like sunglasses is linearly polarized (8.2).

book_ref.quote: Example is the light passing through a polarizing filter, like sunglasses.

blocks.prompt: 18 Circularly polarized light whose electric field rotates clockwise is called:
blocks.explanation: Clockwise rotation is right-handed and counterclockwise is left-handed circular polarization (8.2).

book_ref.quote: When the electric field rotates circularly, either clockwise (right-handed)

blocks.prompt: 19 Light reflected off a CD or DVD is given as an example of:
blocks.explanation: The chapter gives light reflected off a CD or DVD as an example of circular polarization (8.2).

book_ref.quote: Example is the light reflected off a CD

blocks.prompt: 20 A combination of linear and circular polarization in which the electric field vector traces an elliptical path is:
blocks.explanation: When E traces an elliptical path the light is elliptically polarized (8.2).

book_ref.quote: the electric field vector traces an elliptical path is called elliptical polarization

blocks.prompt: 21 In elliptical polarization, the two components Ex and Ey of the electric field:

options.text: are unequal and/or differ in phase by an arbitrary angle
are always equal and in phase
are parallel to the direction of propagation

blocks.explanation: In elliptical polarization Ex and Ey are not equal and/or differ in phase by an arbitrary angle θ (8.2).

book_ref.quote: are not equal and/or they differ in phase by an arbitrary angle

blocks.prompt: 22 Light passing through a stress plate or a waveplate is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Light through a stress plate or waveplate is the chapter's example of elliptical polarization (8.2).

book_ref.quote: Example is the light passing through a stress plate or a waveplate.

blocks.prompt: 23 How many basic types of polarization of light are described in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: The basic types are linear, circular and elliptical polarization (8.2).

book_ref.quote: Here are the basic types of polarization of light.

blocks.text: 8.3 Production and detection of plane polarized light

blocks.prompt: 24 Light from an ordinary incandescent bulb is unpolarized because its electrical vibrations are:
blocks.explanation: The bulb's (and the Sun's) light is unpolarized because its vibrations are randomly oriented (8.3).

book_ref.quote: is unpolarized, because its (electrical) vibrations are randomly oriented in space

blocks.prompt: 25 When unpolarized light falls on a sheet of polaroid, the transmitted light is:
blocks.explanation: Unpolarized light incident on a polaroid (polarizer) is transmitted as plane polarized light (8.3).

book_ref.quote: If unpolarized light is made incident on a sheet of polaroid (polarizer)

blocks.prompt: 26 In the two-polaroid experiment, the second polaroid which is rotated is called the:
blocks.explanation: The first polaroid is the polarizer and the second, rotated one is the analyzer (8.3).

book_ref.quote: If the second polaroid (analyzer) is slowly rotated about the beam of light

blocks.prompt: 27 Light emerging from the analyzer disappears when the axes of polarizer and analyzer are:
blocks.explanation: As the analyzer is rotated the light dims and disappears when the axes become mutually perpendicular (8.3).

book_ref.quote: disappears when the axes become mutually perpendicular

blocks.prompt: 28 The light through the analyzer is brightest when the axes of the two polaroids are:
blocks.explanation: On further rotation the light reappears and is brightest when the axes are parallel again (8.3).

book_ref.quote: becomes brightest when the axes are again parallel to each other

blocks.prompt: 29 The experiment with a polarizer and a rotating analyzer proves that light waves are:
blocks.explanation: The disappearance of light at crossed polaroids proves that light waves are transverse (8.3).

book_ref.quote: This experiment proves that light waves are transverse waves.

blocks.prompt: 30 If light waves were longitudinal, then with two mutually perpendicular polaroids the light would:
blocks.explanation: Longitudinal waves would never disappear even with mutually perpendicular polaroids (8.3).

book_ref.quote: If the light waves were longitudinal, they would never disappear

blocks.prompt: 31 Light reflected from the smooth surface of water is:

options.text: partially polarized parallel to the surface

blocks.explanation: The Ponder Upon box: light reflected from smooth water is partially polarized parallel to the surface (8.3).

book_ref.quote: Light reflected from smooth surface of water is partially polarized parallel to the surface.

blocks.text: 8.4 Polarized light by the method of reflection

blocks.prompt: 32 The angle of incidence on a transparent medium at which the reflected light is almost plane polarized is called the:
blocks.explanation: That particular angle of incidence is the polarizing angle θp (8.4).

book_ref.quote: The particular angle of incidence on a transparent medium when the reflected light is almost plane polarized

blocks.prompt: 33 At the polarizing angle, the angle between the reflected and the refracted beams is:
blocks.explanation: At the polarizing angle the reflected and refracted beams are at right angle, so θp + θr = 90° (8.4).

book_ref.quote: the reflected and refracted beams are at right angle to each other at the polarizing angle

blocks.prompt: 34 Brewster's law for light going from medium 1 (refractive index n1) to medium 2 (refractive index n2) is:
blocks.explanation: From n1 sin θp = n2 cos θp we get tan θp = n2/n1, Brewster's law (8.4).

book_ref.quote: This equation is known as Brewster's law.

blocks.prompt: 35 When medium 1 is air, Brewster's law states that the tangent of the polarizing angle is equal to:

options.text: the speed of light in medium 2
the reciprocal of the refractive index

blocks.explanation: With n1 = 1 for air, tan θp = n, the refractive index of the second medium (8.4).

book_ref.quote: the tangent of the angle of polarization is numerically equal to the refractive index

blocks.prompt: 36 The polarizing angle, at which the reflected and refracted rays are at 90°, is also called the:
blocks.explanation: The angle θp at which the reflected and refracted rays make 90° is also called the Brewster angle θB (8.4).

book_ref.quote: is also called the Brewster angle

blocks.prompt: 37 Light in air falls at the polarizing angle on a material of refractive index 1.6. The polarizing angle is about:

book_ref.quote: A beam of light strikes the surface of a plate of glass with a refractive index

blocks.prompt: 38 Light in air strikes a medium of refractive index 1.8 at the polarizing angle. The angle of refraction is about:
39 The polarizing angle for light in air falling on a transparent medium is 52°. The refractive index of the medium is about:

book_ref.quote: If medium 1 is air, then equation becomes

blocks.prompt: 40 In deriving Brewster's law, sin θr is replaced by cos θp because:

options.text: θr = θp at the polarizing angle
θr = 90° − θp at the polarizing angle
θr = 180° − θp at the polarizing angle

blocks.explanation: Since θp + θr = 90°, sin θr = sin(90° − θp) = cos θp (8.4).

book_ref.quote: Let a beam of unpolarized light be made incident on the surface of medium 2

blocks.prompt: 41 Who discovered in 1808 that polarized light is obtained when ordinary light is reflected by a plane sheet of glass?
blocks.explanation: In 1808 Malus discovered polarization by reflection from a plane sheet of glass (8.4).

book_ref.quote: In 1808, Malus discovered that polarized light is obtained when ordinary light is reflected

blocks.prompt: 42 The most suitable angle of incidence on glass for which the reflected ray becomes plane polarized is about:
blocks.explanation: For glass the most suitable angle of incidence is about 57° (8.4).

book_ref.quote: The most suitable angle of incidence ‘i’ is about 57° for glass

blocks.prompt: 43 When light reflected from glass at about 57° is viewed through a slowly rotated polaroid, it is:
blocks.explanation: The reflected light is practically extinguished at one position of the polaroid, proving it is plane polarized (8.4).

book_ref.quote: the light is practically extinguished at one position of the polaroid

blocks.prompt: 44 Light reflected from the surface of a table becomes darker when viewed through a rotated polaroid. This shows that the reflected light is:
blocks.explanation: Darkening at some positions shows the table's reflected light is partially plane polarized (8.4).

book_ref.quote: Light reflected from the surface of a table becomes darker when viewed through a rotated polaroid

blocks.prompt: 45 Light reflected at the polarizing angle is polarized:

options.text: perpendicular to the plane of incidence

blocks.explanation: Reflected light is polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence, drawn as dots in Fig. 8.6 (8.4).

book_ref.quote: Reflected light is polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence

blocks.prompt: 46 Under optics and photonics, polarization is essential for:

options.text: polarized sunglasses, LCD screens and optical communication systems

blocks.explanation: Polarization is essential for polarized sunglasses, LCD screens and optical communication systems (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Polarization is essential for applications like polarized sunglasses, LCD

blocks.prompt: 47 In imaging and microscopy, polarization enhances image quality mainly by:
blocks.explanation: Polarization reduces glare (unwanted light that interferes with vision) and improves contrast (8.5).

book_ref.quote: reducing glare (unwanted light that interferes with vision)

blocks.prompt: 48 In medicine, polarization is useful because it can:
blocks.explanation: Polarization is used in cancer diagnosis, tissue imaging and laser surgery by distinguishing between tissue types (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Polarization is used in cancer diagnosis, tissue imaging, and laser surgery

blocks.prompt: 49 In astronomy, polarization helps to analyze:

options.text: the mass of the Moon only
light from distant stars and the cosmic microwave background radiation

blocks.explanation: Polarization helps analyze cosmic phenomena such as light from distant stars or the cosmic microwave background (8.5).

book_ref.quote: or the cosmic microwave background radiation

blocks.prompt: 50 The ability of some substances to rotate the plane of polarization of light passing through them is called:
blocks.explanation: Optical activity is the ability of some substances to rotate the plane of polarization (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Optical activity is the ability of some substances to rotate the plane of polarization

blocks.prompt: 51 Which of the following is an optically active substance?
blocks.explanation: Quartz, cinnabar (HgS), sugar water, insulin and collagen are optically active (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Examples are quartz crystals, cinnabar (HgS), sugar water, insulin and collagen.

blocks.prompt: 52 The amount of rotation of the plane of polarization by an optically active substance does NOT depend on:

options.text: the distance light travels through it

blocks.explanation: Rotation depends on the type of substance, its concentration, the distance travelled and the wavelength (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The amount and direction of rotation depends on following factors:

blocks.prompt: 53 Optical activity occurs due to:

options.text: the high temperature of the substance
the colour of the light source
the asymmetric (for example helical) shape of molecules
the reflection of light from the surface

blocks.explanation: Optical activity is due to the asymmetric shape of molecules, such as being helical (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Optical activity occurs due to the asymmetric shape of molecules

blocks.prompt: 54 The optical rotation of sugar in solution can be used to determine its:
blocks.explanation: The property of optically active substances can be used to determine their concentration in solutions (8.5).

book_ref.quote: This property of optically active substances can be used to determine their concentration

blocks.prompt: 55 A few millimetre thickness of an optically active crystal rotates the plane of polarization by:
blocks.explanation: A few millimetre thickness of such crystals rotates the plane of polarization by many degrees (8.5).

book_ref.quote: A few millimetre thickness of such crystals will rotate the plane of polarization by many degrees

blocks.prompt: 56 A sugar solution placed between crossed polarizer and analyzer lets some light through because it:

options.text: changes the speed of light to zero
rotates the plane of polarization by an angle θ

blocks.explanation: Sugar solution rotates the plane of polarization by an angle θ, so the analyzer must be turned to stop the light again (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The analyzer thus stops the light when rotated from the vertical

blocks.prompt: 57 Polarized light of intensity 64 W m⁻² passes through an analyzer whose axis is at 30° to the polarizer's axis. The emerging intensity is:

book_ref.quote: Polarized light with an intensity of 75 W m⁻² passes through an analyzer

blocks.prompt: 58 Polarized light of amplitude 12 units meets an analyzer whose axis is at 60° to its plane of polarization. The transmitted amplitude is:

book_ref.quote: A polarized light with an amplitude of 5 units passes through a polarizer

blocks.prompt: 59 The polarizing angle for light from air on a liquid is 50°. Its refractive index is about:
blocks.explanation: n = tan θp = tan 50° = 1.19 (Example 8.2 method).

book_ref.quote: Find the refractive index of a medium if polarizing angle is 54.5°.

blocks.prompt: 60 When we look through two polarizers that are crossed:
blocks.explanation: Looking through two crossed polarizers, very little light passes through (Do you know? box, 8.5).

book_ref.quote: Looking through two polarizers when they are

blocks.prompt: 61 The two main applications of polarizers described in the chapter are:

options.text: sky photography and stress analysis of materials

blocks.explanation: The two main applications are sky photography and stress analysis of materials (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Polarizers, also known as polarizing filters, have two main applications:

blocks.prompt: 62 In sky photography, the glare and haze reduced by a polarizer are produced by:

options.text: reflection of light from the camera lens
scattering of light by small particles in the atmosphere

blocks.explanation: Glare and haze come from scattering of light by small particles in the atmosphere (8.5).

book_ref.quote: polarizers are used to reduce the glare and haze which are produced by the scattering of light

blocks.prompt: 63 Analysing the stress patterns in a transparent material by shining polarized light through it is known as:
blocks.explanation: The technique is known as photoelasticity, widely used in engineering and quality control (8.5).

book_ref.quote: and is widely used in fields like engineering, materials science, and quality control

blocks.prompt: 64 When a material under polarized light is stressed, its changed molecular structure produces:

options.text: interference fringes giving information about the material
a change in the speed of light in air

blocks.explanation: Stress changes the molecular structure and the interaction with light, forming interference fringes that give information about the material (8.5).

book_ref.quote: When a material is stressed, its molecular structure changes

blocks.prompt: 65 Stress analysis of a transparent material with polarized light can help researchers to:

options.text: increase the mass of the material

blocks.explanation: Researchers can determine stress patterns, identify weaknesses or defects and analyze optical properties (8.5).

book_ref.quote: identify potential weaknesses or defects

blocks.prompt: 66 According to Malus's law, the intensity of plane polarized light after passing through an analyzer is directly proportional to:
blocks.explanation: Malus's law: I ∝ cos²θ, where θ is the angle between the transmission axes of analyzer and polarizer (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Malus's law states that the intensity I of plane polarized light after passing through an analyzer

blocks.prompt: 67 In Malus's law I = I₀cos²θ, the quantity I₀ is the intensity of:

options.text: the polarized light incident on the analyzer (after the polarizer)
the light absorbed by the analyzer
the light reflected by the analyzer

blocks.explanation: I₀ is the intensity of the incident polarized light, after passing through the polarizer (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Intensity of the incident polarized light (after passing through a polarizer)

blocks.prompt: 68 An analyzer is:

options.text: a mirror that reflects light at 57°
a polarizer placed after another polarizer

blocks.explanation: An analyzer is also a polarizer that is placed after a polarizer (8.5).

book_ref.quote: An analyzer is also a polarizer that is placed after a polarizer.

blocks.prompt: 69 Transparent crystalline materials like tourmaline that confine vibrations of light to only one plane are called:
blocks.explanation: Materials like tourmaline and calcite that confine vibrations to one plane are called polaroids (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Such materials are called polaroids which have high directionality in crystal structure.

blocks.prompt: 70 Which natural phenomena can also polarize light?
blocks.explanation: Light can also be polarized naturally by reflection, refraction and scattering (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Light can also be polarized by natural phenomena like reflection, refraction and scattering.

blocks.prompt: 71 When a polaroid is rotated in front of a polarized ray, the transmitted intensity varies because of:

options.text: the angle between the axes of the first polarizer and the second polarizer
the change in the speed of light
the change in the colour of the light

blocks.explanation: The variation of intensity is caused by the angle between the initial polarizer and the axis of the second polarizer (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The reason that causes the variation of intensity is the angle between the initial polarizer

blocks.prompt: 72 When polarized light of amplitude A₀ strikes an analyzer at angle θ, the component absorbed in the analyzer is:
blocks.explanation: A₀ is resolved into A₀cos θ (passes) and A₀sin θ (absorbed in the analyzer) (8.5).

book_ref.quote: The component A₀sinθ is absorbed in the analyzer.

blocks.prompt: 73 In deriving Malus's law, the intensity of light is taken as:

options.text: the square root of the amplitude

blocks.explanation: Intensity is the square of the amplitude, I = A², so I = A₀²cos²θ = I₀cos²θ (8.5).

book_ref.quote: Since intensity I is the square of the amplitude A it can be expressed as:

blocks.prompt: 74 According to Malus's law, the light is completely extinguished when the angle between the axes of polarizer and analyzer is:
blocks.explanation: If θ = 90°, then I = I₀cos²90° = 0 (8.5).

book_ref.quote: This means the light is extinguished completely

blocks.prompt: 75 When θ = 0° in Malus's law, the intensity transmitted through the analyzer is:
blocks.explanation: If θ = 0°, then I = I₀cos²0° = I₀ (8.5).

book_ref.quote: This means the intensity transmitted through the analyzer is equal to the initial light intensity

blocks.prompt: 76 Polarized light of intensity 120 W m⁻² falls on an analyzer whose axis makes 45° with the polarizer's axis. The transmitted intensity is:

book_ref.quote: Rotation of the analyzer affects the intensity of the polarized light.

blocks.prompt: 77 Polarized light of intensity 200 W m⁻² passes through an analyzer set at 60° to the polarizer. The intensity transmitted is:

book_ref.quote: It is used to further reduce the intensity of light and also adjust it

blocks.prompt: 78 Through what angle between the axes of polarizer and analyzer will the transmitted intensity be 75% of I₀?

book_ref.quote: Actually, Malus's law gives a mathematical relation between the intensity of the light incident

blocks.prompt: 79 If the amplitude of light passing through an analyzer becomes half of the incident amplitude, the transmitted intensity is:
blocks.explanation: A = A₀/2 means cos θ = 0.5 (θ = 60°), and I = A² gives I = I₀/4 (8.5).

book_ref.quote: When the incident polarized light of amplitude A₀ strikes the analyzer at an angle

blocks.prompt: 80 A gravitational wave can be observed by measuring:

options.text: the change in colour of light
the change in length between two objects

blocks.explanation: A gravitational wave is a stretching and compressing of space, observed by measuring the change in length between two objects (8.6).

book_ref.quote: A gravitational wave is a stretching and compressing of space

blocks.prompt: 81 Gravitational waves are:

options.text: waves on the surface of the oceans
longitudinal waves in the Earth's crust
ripples in the fabric of spacetime produced by violent cosmic events

blocks.explanation: GWs are ripples in the fabric of spacetime produced by violent cosmic events like colliding black holes (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Ripples in the fabric of spacetime, produced by violent cosmic events

blocks.prompt: 82 Gravitational waves travel with:
blocks.explanation: GWs travel at the speed of light, carrying information about their source (8.6).

book_ref.quote: that travel at the speed of light, carrying information about their source

blocks.prompt: 83 In the pond analogy of gravitational waves, the water surface stands for:
blocks.explanation: The water surface represents spacetime, the stone the cosmic event, and the shore the observatories (8.6).

book_ref.quote: If we throw a stone into a pond, the stone creates ripples on the water surface

blocks.prompt: 84 Gravitational waves of the same frequency and amplitude produced by a single massive object, such as a neutron star, spinning at a constant rate are:
blocks.explanation: A single massive object spinning at a constant rate produces continuous GWs with the same frequency and amplitude (8.6).

book_ref.quote: When a single massive object spins with a constant rate, such as a neutron star

blocks.prompt: 85 Gravitational waves produced by violent events like supernovae and gamma-ray bursts are called:
blocks.explanation: Burst GWs are produced by violent events like supernovae, gamma-ray bursts or cosmic strings (8.6).

book_ref.quote: These are produced by violent events like supernovae, gamma-ray bursts, or cosmic strings.

blocks.prompt: 86 Which type of gravitational waves is the most difficult to detect?
blocks.explanation: Stochastic GWs are weak random signals from many weak sources and are the most difficult to detect (8.6).

book_ref.quote: These GWs are the most difficult to detect.

blocks.prompt: 87 Gravitational waves from two neutron stars or black holes orbiting and spiralling in towards each other are called:
blocks.explanation: Binary neutron stars or black holes orbiting each other produce compact binary inspiral GWs (8.6).

book_ref.quote: compact inspiral GWs are produced

blocks.prompt: 88 Gravitational waves from vehicles and airplanes on the Earth cannot be detected because:

options.text: they do not accelerate at all
their masses and accelerations are too small

blocks.explanation: Every accelerating object produces GWs, but masses and accelerations on the Earth are too small to give detectable waves (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Every physical object that accelerates, produces gravitational waves.

blocks.prompt: 89 LIGO, which detects gravitational waves, is situated in:
blocks.explanation: LIGO is situated in the USA; Virgo is in Cascina, Italy (8.6).

book_ref.quote: which is situated in USA and Virgo

blocks.prompt: 90 As gravitational waves travel away from their source, their intensity:
blocks.explanation: The waves propagate through the universe, weakening in intensity as they get farther from the source (8.6).

book_ref.quote: The waves propagate through the universe, weakening in intensity

blocks.prompt: 91 An orbit with eccentricity ε between 0 and 1 (0 < ε < 1) is:
blocks.explanation: From the eccentricity table: ε = 0 circular, 0 < ε < 1 elliptical, ε = 1 parabolic, ε > 1 hyperbolic (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Eccentricity ε is a measure of the amount by which an object deviates from a perfect circle.

blocks.prompt: 92 A body whose path has eccentricity ε = 1.4 follows:
blocks.explanation: ε > 1 means a hyperbolic trajectory (eccentricity table, 8.6).

book_ref.quote: deviates from a perfect circle

blocks.prompt: 93 Which of the following is NOT listed as a property on which the characteristics of gravitational waves depend?
blocks.explanation: GW characteristics depend on the masses, the orbital period and frequency, and the eccentricity of the orbit (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Orbital period and frequency

blocks.prompt: 94 Gravitational waves are a prediction of:
blocks.explanation: GWs are a prediction of Einstein's theory of general relativity, initially predicted in 1916 (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Gravitational waves are a prediction of Einstein's theory of general relativity

blocks.prompt: 95 According to Einstein's general theory of relativity, gravity is:

options.text: a curvature of spacetime caused by massive bodies

blocks.explanation: Gravity is not a force but a curvature of spacetime caused by massive bodies, like a dent in a mattress (8.6).

book_ref.quote: gravity is not a force, but a curvature of spacetime caused by massive bodies

blocks.prompt: 96 Gravitational waves were predicted by Albert Einstein in:
blocks.explanation: Einstein initially predicted gravitational waves in 1916 (8.6).

book_ref.quote: as initially predicted by Albert Einstein in 1916

blocks.prompt: 97 The first gravitational waves detected (on 14 September 2015) came from:
blocks.explanation: The first detected GWs came from two merging black holes; waves from colliding neutron stars were first detected in 2017 (8.6, 8.7).

book_ref.quote: Waves from colliding neutron stars were first detected in 2017.

blocks.prompt: 98 A binary system, in the context of gravitational waves, consists of:

options.text: two compact objects orbiting each other and emitting gravitational waves
a star and its single planet at rest

blocks.explanation: A binary system is two compact objects (black holes, neutron stars or white dwarfs) orbiting each other and emitting GWs (8.6).

book_ref.quote: A system consisting of two compact objects, such as black holes, neutron stars, or white dwarfs

blocks.prompt: 99 Dr. Nergis Mavalvala, a Pakistani-American astrophysicist at MIT, is known for her work on:
blocks.explanation: Dr. Nergis Mavalvala is known for her work on gravitational waves (8.6).

book_ref.quote: Pakistani-American Astrophysicist at MIT known for her work on gravitational waves

blocks.prompt: 100 The periodic stretching and compressing of a body caused by a passing gravitational wave is known as:
blocks.explanation: Periodic stretching and compressing of a body is spacetime distortion, known as tidal forces (8.6).

book_ref.quote: This effect is known as “tidal forces”

blocks.prompt: 101 A passing gravitational wave stretches and compresses a body in the direction:

blocks.prompt: 106 Compared with a conventional interferometer, LIGO is about:

blocks.prompt: 108 In a gravitational wave interferometer, the component that divides the LASER beam into two perpendicular beams is the:

blocks.prompt: 109 The purpose of the Fabry Perot cavity in a gravitational wave interferometer is to:

blocks.prompt: 110 The returning beams in a gravitational wave interferometer, and any tiny phase shifts, are measured by:

blocks.prompt: 111 The mirror that continually reflects LASER light that has already travelled through the instrument back into the interferometer is the:

blocks.prompt: 112 When a gravitational wave passes through an interferometer, it produces between the two beams a:
